about: Backshell (afterbody) heating as a share of the stagnation-point heating of the heat shield, and the backshell TPS sizing point.

Mars.about: Mars 2020 flight (MEDLI2): peak total heat flux on the backshell 4.47 W/cm2 (thermocouple plug), 5.10 W/cm2 (heat flux gauge), 6.01 W/cm2 (Kalman blend of the three co-located sensors; 0.86 convective + 5.16 radiative). The simulator's own Sutton-Graves stagnation heating on the Mars 2020 reconstructed trajectory peaks at 54.5 W/cm2 (t = 76.8 s, Edquist et al. 2022 Table 4). 4.47 to 6.01 over 54.5 is 0.082 to 0.110; 0.10 is used. CO2 radiation in the wake carries most of it, so the share does not fall with the convective heating.
sources: K. T. Edquist et al., 'Mars 2020 Reconstructed Aerothermal Environments', AIAA SciTech 2022, NTRS 20210024709, Table 4 (p. 15) and Section V.B (p. 22).
Data fusion of in-flight aerothermodynamic heating measurements using Kalman filtering, NTRS 20220006196, Section III (peak values quoted in the abstract and results).
R. A. Miller et al., 'Aftbody Heat Flux Measurements During Mars 2020 Entry', J. Spacecraft Rockets, 2023, doi:10.2514/1.A35783.
Mars.check: MSL design: laminar afterbody heating 3% of the laminar forebody nose (Edquist, AIAA 2005-4817), times 3 for the 200% design uncertainty (Edquist et al. AIAA 2009-4078, Eq. 1) is 9%.

Earth.about: Laminar convective afterbody heating near 3% of the forebody nose (Edquist, AIAA 2005-4817, for MSL). Earth afterbody radiation is smaller than in CO2. Not checked against Earth flight data in this PR.

sizing.about: MSL backshell, SLA-561V: 0.32 in (8.1 mm) needed at the heatshield/backshell seal for the design heat load of 377 J/cm2 (6.3 W/cm2 peak) to keep the bondline below its limit; 0.5 in was flown (Edquist et al. AIAA 2009-4078, NTRS 20090024230, Section E, p. 9). The needed areal mass scales with the heat load to the same power as the heat shield correlation (data.TPS_EXPONENT = 0.51575).
